subject: general
question: A shopkeeper sold some articles at ₹77/- each and earned a profit of 40%. What would be the selling price of each article if the profit is 6%?
solution:
**Given:**

Selling price (SP) with 40% profit = ₹77

Profit percentage = 40%

New profit percentage = 6%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP / (1 + Profit %)

New Selling Price (New SP) = CP × (1 + New Profit %)

**Calculation:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) be x.

SP = CP × (1 + Profit %)

77 = x × (1 + 40/100)

77 = x × 1.40

⇒ x = 77 / 1.40

⇒ x = 55

New SP = CP × (1 + New Profit %)

New SP = 55 × (1 + 6/100)

New SP = 55 × 1.06

New SP = 58.3

**The selling price of each article if the profit is 6% is ₹58.30.**
